questions.question:
Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence.

Pritam said, "The prisoner had slept throughout the journey."

options.text: Pritam said that the prisoner had been sleeping throughout the journey.
Pritam said that the prisoner had sleep throughout the journey.
Pritam said that the prisoner had slept throughout the journey.
Pritam said that the prisoner has slept throughout the journey.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'Option 3'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **When converting** direct speech into reported speech, the tense of the verb usually moves one step back in time. This is known as backshifting.
 
• However, if the **direct speech is in the past perfect** (as is the case with "The prisoner had slept throughout the journey"), it does not change when turned into reported speech because the** past perfect tense is already **the most 'remote' tense possible in English.
 
• So** "had slept"** remains "had slept" in reported speech.

Therefore, the** correct answer **is:* 'Pritam said that the prisoner had slept throughout the journey.'*

questions.question:
Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose ‘No error’.

Bushfire have created havoc and exacerbated the conditions of animals in the forest.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'Option 1'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The **error is in **the part: "Bushfire have created havoc"
 
• The **correct form** should be "Bushfires have created havoc".
 
• In English, **subject-verb agreement** is a grammatical rule which states that the subject and verb must agree in number.
 
• That means, if the subject is plural, the verb must be plural.
 
• Conversely, if the **subject is singular, the verb must be singular.**
 
• In this case, **"Bushfire" **is a singular noun, but **"have" **is a plural verb, so they don't agree in number.
 
• The **sentence should be corrected by** changing "Bushfire" to the plural form "Bushfires" to match the plural verb "have".

Therefore, the **correct sentence** is: *'Bushfires have created havoc and exacerbated the conditions of animals in the forest.'*

questions.question:
Select the correct passive form of the given sentence.

Picasso painted Guernica in 1937.

options.text: Guernica was painting by Picasso in 1937.
Guernica was been painted by Picasso in 1937.
Guernica was paint by Picasso in 1937.
Guernica was painted by Picasso in 1937.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'Option 4'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the active sentence "Picasso painted Guernica in 1937", the** subject** is "Picasso", the **verb** is "painted" (simple past tense) and the **object** is "Guernica".
 
• **When transforming **an active sentence to passive, the object of the active sentence (Guernica) becomes the subject of the passive sentence, the verb form changes to the passive form (was painted), and the subject of the active sentence (Picasso) follows "by".

Therefore, the **correct sentence **is:* 'Guernica was painted by Picasso in 1937.'*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Here are the explanations for the other options:
 
 
• **"Guernica was painting by Picasso in 1937.**" This is incorrect because "painting" is not the past participle form of the verb "paint". The correct past participle is "painted".
 
• **"Guernica was been painted by Picasso in 1937."** This is incorrect because the verb form "was been painted" does not exist in English grammar. The correct form is "was painted".
 
• **"Guernica was paint by Picasso in 1937."** This is incorrect because "paint" is not the past participle form of the verb "paint". The correct past participle is "painted".

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In this context, **"health"** refers to the overall state of the heart, both physically and mentally.
 
• The **sentence talks about **studies that prove the positive impact travel can have on our heart's health, which fits perfectly into the context.

Therefore, the correct sentence is: *Improving your well-being is considered to be the fundamental benefit of travelling. Travelling helps to decrease the risks of heart disease and anxiety while developing our brain health. There have been studies proving that travel can have a positive impact on our heart** health**. The health benefit of travelling is that when you travel to new surroundings you (4) ________ a restart button to your body and mind. This brings in fresh energy when you get back to your normal (5) ________ activities.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Let's consider the other options:
 
 
• **"Bloom"** refers to the process of a flower opening or a person or thing flourishing. It doesn't fit here because we are discussing the health of the heart, not its blooming or flourishing.
 
• **"Pace"** refers to the speed or rate at which something happens or moves. In this context, it doesn't make sense to discuss the pace of the heart when we are discussing overall health benefits.
 
• **"Being" **generally refers to existence or the nature of something. While the heart certainly exists and has a nature, it doesn't fit the context, which is about health.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'Option 1' **i.e.** 'Press'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In this context, **"press" **is the most suitable word because it refers to pushing a button.
 
• Here,** the phrase "press a restart button"** is a metaphorical way of saying that traveling provides a fresh start or a rejuvenation for the body and mind.

Therefore, the **correct sentence** is: *Improving your well-being is considered to be the fundamental benefit of travelling. Travelling helps to decrease the risks of heart disease and anxiety **while** developing our brain health. There have been studies proving that travel can have a positive impact on our heart health. The health benefit of travelling is that when you travel to new surroundings you **press **a restart button to your body and mind. This brings in fresh energy when you get back to your normal (5) ________ activities.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Let's consider the other options:
 
 
• **"Heap"** typically means to pile or stack up something. It doesn't fit here as we can't heap a button.
 
• **"Usurp" **means to take over or seize power unrightfully. It doesn't make sense in this context because it doesn't relate to the act of resetting or starting over.
 
• **"Snatch" **means to quickly seize or grab something. While you could theoretically snatch a button, it doesn't convey the intended meaning of initiating a fresh start or reset.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** 'Option 1' **i.e.** 'Regular'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In this context, **"regular" **is used to describe the usual or ordinary activities someone engages in.
 
• **It contrasts with** the new and different experiences associated with traveling, providing a standard or baseline that traveling helps to rejuvenate.

Therefore, the **correct sentence** is: *Improving your well-being is considered to be the fundamental benefit of travelling. Travelling helps to decrease the risks of heart disease and anxiety while developing our brain health. There have been studies proving that travel can have a positive impact on our heart health. The health benefit of travelling is that when you travel to new surroundings you press a restart button to your body and mind. This brings in fresh energy when you get back to your normal **regular** activities.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Here's why the other options aren't as suitable:
 
 
• **"Sedentary" **refers to a lifestyle with little to no physical activity. Although it could theoretically fit, it connotes a negative or unhealthy lifestyle, which isn't necessarily implied in the passage.
 
• **"Arbitrate" **means to reach an authoritative judgement or settlement, and it doesn't fit the context of daily activities at all.
 
• **"Moderate"** could potentially work if it were describing the intensity of the activities, but without that context,** "regular"** is a more broadly applicable choice.
